rules.statement: When an end user changes their own password, end every other session of that principal but keep the session that made the change, and revoke every grant that was issued outside any session.
rules.why: OWASP ASVS V3.3.3 and NIST SP 800-63B require the other sessions to end after a password change. Keeping the current session leaves the device that proved the change signed in, and revoking sessionless grants means no grant outlives the credential it was issued under.
rules.check: Look at the success path of a password-change handler. Report it if it ends no sessions, ends all sessions including the current one, or leaves grants that belong to no session active.

rules.statement: End the other sessions after a password change through the per-session termination path, which claims each session and notifies its relying parties. Don't revoke every grant outside the current session with a single exclusion filter.
rules.why: A single exclusion filter revokes the sessions' grants without telling their relying parties, so they get no back-channel logout.
rules.check: Look for a password change or 'sign out everywhere else' that bulk-revokes grants with a filter instead of dispatching a termination for each session.

rules.statement: Run a password change in this order: verify the current password under the failed-attempt limit, confirm that the verified account is the same account as the signed-in principal, judge the new password with the shared password policy, then save it in one unit of work.
rules.why: The current password must count against the per-account attempt limit, the change must not land on a different account, and every password is judged by one policy wherever it is set.
rules.check: In a password-change implementation, report a current-password check that skips the attempt gate, a missing check that the verified account ID equals the principal's account, a missing password-policy check, or saves spread across more than one unit of work.

rules.statement: Encode password strings into pooled secure-memory buffers (such as `SecureMemoryPool` from `NCode.Buffers`), not into ordinary arrays.
rules.why: The source requires both the current and the new password to be encoded into `SecureMemoryPool` buffers.
rules.check: Look for code that turns passwords into bytes with `Encoding.GetBytes` into a plain `byte[]` or an `ArrayPool` buffer.

rules.statement: When a capability is optional for pluggable backends, define it as a separate seam. Register a default that reports 'not supported' with `TryAdd*`, and have each backend that supports it replace that registration so the result is the same whatever order the registration methods are called in.
rules.why: A backend that cannot support the capability (for example, a passwordless backend asked to change a password) just says so. A required member on a shared interface would force most implementations to give an answer they cannot give.
rules.check: Report a member added to a shared backend interface that most implementations cannot honour. Also report a default registered with a plain `Add*`, or a backend override that only takes effect when it is called before or after the default.

rules.statement: Run security effects that follow a committed change, such as ending other sessions, on their own bounded cancellation token, not on the request's token.
rules.why: Once the change is committed, the effects that follow it must still run if the request is aborted, and the bounded token stops them from running forever.
rules.check: Look for post-commit calls such as session termination that are passed `HttpContext.RequestAborted` or the request's cancellation token.

rules.statement: Make self-service account pages require an active session for both GET and POST, and redirect to the login page when there is none.
rules.why: A self-service change must be tied to an authenticated session, and that session is the one that survives the change.
rules.check: Look for account self-service endpoints whose GET or POST handler does not check for an active session before it acts.
